name: Driftwood
title: Race to a faster first demo
subtitle: How I got new clients at driftwood, an a16z speedrun startup, to their first demo in 7 business days.
tagline: Driftwood was refunding more than half its revenue. A shorter onboarding on the founder's call, a storyboard editor, and a calmer dashboard got new clients to their first demo in 7 business days.

main.alt: The redesigned driftwood Home: Pipeline with sent, opened, replies and meetings booked

sections.heading: Driftwood was losing more than half its revenue to refunds

blocks.text: Clients paid, then waited about a month for their first custom demos. **One churned. Aayush refunded four others before they asked, to keep them from churning as well.**

text: driftwood is an AI cold outbound agent. Every cold message it sends carries **a working demo of the client's product, built for that prospect.**
The founder, Aayush, was signing clients fast and **onboarding each one by hand with coding agents.** He was scaling quickly. However…

sections.heading: Getting a client to their first demo took 2.5–3 weeks

blocks.text: In an internal audit with the founders, the refunds traced back to **how long it took to get a client going.**

blocks.text: Aayush put it simply: clients have **the most intent in their first week.**

blocks.heading: Initial founder feedback
items: Too much back and forth for the pilot demo
About **6 rounds of revisions** on average, over Slack, between the founder and clients, across **2 weeks.**
Critical setup was missing
**60% had cloned their face**, after 1–2 weeks and 3–4 reminders.
The dashboard overwhelmed people
**12 menu items**, with tabs inside tabs and no clear visual hierarchy.
Onboarding was manual
Aayush set up every client by hand, and **he was signing more clients.**

blocks.text: I spoke with **6 of driftwood's 8 clients** about where they got stuck. Hover a card to see the theme it fed.

blocks.note: Paraphrased from client calls, including the offboarding call with the one client who churned.

items.text: The dashboard **overwhelmed me**, and I **couldn't find things.**
The timeline to get demos booked was **too long.** We needed to **move faster.**
I wish **editing the pilot demo** was quicker.
It felt **messy and unusable.** Honestly, I don't know **how my demos are doing** and which ones are going better.
I needed time to **look okay on camera**, and then I **forgot about it** a few times. I had other stuff going on.
Revisions went back and forth over Slack, and it just **felt inefficient.**

blocks.text: How might we get new clients to __their first great demo faster__, so they feel they're getting what they paid for?

blocks.title: A storyboard editor for the pilot demo
bullets: Clients approve, change or cut each shot themselves, **in place of Slack threads.**
First a single mic for every change. Clients wanted finer control, so each section got **its own editor, with typing and a mic.**

frame.alt: The storyboard editor: one shot open, with Says and On screen, each with its own mic

blocks.label: What we learned
blocks.text: Aayush wanted onboarding to feel personal, so we kept it an **in-person, live experience** that the founder talks through on the call, **with a flow to guide it.** Only the pilot demo needed to be async. **The trade-off:** face cloning moved out of onboarding, and we couldn't afford to lose days waiting on it, so I designed ways to make sure **it didn't slip through the cracks.**

sections.heading: V2: we took face cloning out of onboarding. So where does it go?

blocks.text: **Assumption:** clients have the most intent right after the kickoff call, so if the ask lands then, **they will set up their face on their own.**

items.why: 60% did it, after 1–2 weeks and 3–4 reminders.
Aayush explains it in person, but clients can't film on a call or without good light.
Aayush builds the trust in person. Clients record when they're ready, at the top of their inbox.

blocks.title: The email lands right after the call
bullets: One card, two buttons: **Set up**, or **Remind me tomorrow.**
We tried "Set up" alone and saw **2 people open the email and leave it.** "Remind me tomorrow" brings it back to the top of their inbox at a better time, so we didn't have to chase them.

frame.alt: The face and voice email: a talking welcome in the porthole, then Set up or Remind me tomorrow

blocks.text: From 60% in 1–2 weeks to **every client in 2–3 days.**
Onboarded **6 new clients.** First demo in **7 business days**, down from 2.5–3 weeks.

sections.heading: Where I overrode the AI, on logic and on looks

blocks.text: I designed in the production codebase with Claude Code. **66 logged iterations**, each with screenshots and a trade-offs log. These are the moments I said no.

items.said: The lighting on my face is not actually good right now. Fix how it evaluates that.
items.ai: A light check that averaged the middle of the camera frame, so a lit wall behind a dim face passed.
items.shipped: It reads only the skin inside the face oval and fails light from behind or the side. It holds for every skin tone.

items.said: the voice thing for the lead list shouldn't be in onboarding.
items.ai: A chat box on the onboarding leads step, to type out who you want to reach.
items.shipped: Most clients already keep their leads in a sheet, as the founder pointed out, so onboarding only uploads one. Typing who to reach moved to the main dashboard.

items.said: is create your first demo the right cta? becuase theyre waiting on the team to help put it together
items.ai: The last step ended on Create demo, implying an instant, self-made demo.
items.shipped: Start pilot: our team makes your first demos and emails you when they're ready.

items.said: Too hyper realistic on the all hands thing and I think you need to drop the wheel. The concept isn't premium.
items.ai: A lit 3D helm with a spin, a light sweep and sparkles on every invite.
items.shipped: A plain Invite your team step: emails as chips you can remove, then Start pilot.

items.said: its so sudden right now. its giving me a seizure.
items.ai: Publish switched the page from light to dark in a single frame.
items.shipped: One even fade over 900ms on the card's own easing. No sudden dark or flash.

items.label: Days iterating on the pilot demo

tools.title: I code tools for myself when I'm blocked
tools.text: Describing a copy fix, a screen swap or where a callout sits made prompts long and slow, so I built **Edit text**, **Swap image** and **callouts** to do them by hand in seconds.

track.title: I track my hours and iterations to design better
track.text: Every screen was captured at every iteration, with the prompt behind it, so I can see **how many tries each screen took**, where I lost time, and why.
track.stat: 66 iterations · 2,868 screenshots · 6 days · a median 24 minutes between tries
track.note: One iteration can touch several parts. Tagged from the prompt and title of each iteration.

items: Frame a problem by what it costs
This was retention and usage **before it was onboarding.**
Understand the business before the flow
I designed fully async when **only the pilot demo needed to be.**
